name: Cloud & DevOps
blurb: Ship and run apps: hosting choice, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD, Cloudflare, GCP, AWS, Azure and observability.
searches: GitHub Actions security OIDC best practice update
Cloudflare Workers Cloud Run Lambda new feature announcement
Kubernetes release deprecation pod security change
agent skill DevOps deploy Claude Terraform Kubernetes

tests.prompt: Write a production Dockerfile and .dockerignore for a Node 22 Express API that builds TypeScript to dist/, then give me the gcloud commands to deploy it to Cloud Run in europe-west1 with a secret API key.
tests.good: Multi-stage build with pinned slim/alpine base, deps cached before source copy, dev deps excluded, numeric non-root user, listens on 0.0.0.0 and $PORT; .dockerignore excludes .git, node_modules and .env; builds for linux/amd64; deploy uses Artifact Registry image, explicit --region, dedicated service account, --set-secrets from Secret Manager (not env literal), asks before --allow-unauthenticated; verification via logs and health check; rollback via traffic to previous revision.

tests.prompt: Set up GitHub Actions for our Terraform repo (AWS, two environments). PRs should show the plan, merges to main should apply to prod.
tests.good: fmt -check, validate, tflint and a security scan (trivy/checkov) on PRs; plan -out uploaded as artifact and summarised on the PR; apply consumes the reviewed plan file (no re-plan) in a protected production environment with required reviewers; AWS auth via OIDC with aud sts.amazonaws.com and sub pinned to repo and branch/environment (no wildcards), no static keys; remote S3 state with locking and separate state per env; pinned versions and committed lock file; scheduled drift detection that alerts rather than auto-applies.

tests.prompt: Our Kubernetes deployment shows pods in CrashLoopBackOff right after a new release. Walk me through finding the cause and getting users back to working.
tests.good: Mitigates first with kubectl rollout undo (or previous image) and checks rollout status; then diagnoses with describe pod events, logs --previous, events sorted by time; checks exit code (137 OOMKilled vs app error), missing env/secret, wrong command/port, overly aggressive liveness probe; compares the diff between releases; suggests readiness/startup probes and resource limits; no destructive steps without confirmation.

tests.prompt: Move our Node API and its Postgres database off a single VPS onto AWS: ECS Fargate for the API, RDS for Postgres, Terraform for all of it, and GitHub Actions to deploy. Make sure no secrets leak along the way.
tests.good: States a short plan first: infra here (platform-choice.md, docker.md, terraform.md, aws.md, ci-cd.md), the database move through backend-databases (postgres-schema.md: forward-only migrations as a release step; query-performance.md: pooling and timeouts), secrets and workflows through security (secrets.md and github-actions.md: secret scanning in CI, actions pinned to a SHA, minimal permissions). Confirms account and region first; applies only a reviewed plan; OIDC to AWS with sub pinned, no static keys; RDS credentials in Secrets Manager, not tfvars; a cutover and rollback plan; checks the Done means of all three crafts and says what wasn't verified.

tests.prompt: I have a Helm chart for my API in charts/api and two clusters, staging and prod. Set up Argo CD so staging deploys automatically whenever main changes, but prod only changes when I press sync. Each environment needs its own values, the database password must not be in git, and tell me exactly how I roll back a bad prod release.
tests.good: Defines the apps as Argo CD Application (or ApplicationSet) manifests with spec.source.helm.valueFiles per environment and a pinned targetRevision (tag or SHA for prod, not a floating branch); Staging has syncPolicy.automated (prune and selfHeal) while prod has no automated sync, so release is a manual sync; Uses an AppProject to restrict source repos, destinations and namespaces rather than the default project; Keeps the DB password out of git via External Secrets Operator, Sealed Secrets or SOPS, and says plainly that values files and Helm templates must not carry it; Gives a rollback that is correct for GitOps: git revert and sync (or argocd app rollback only because prod auto-sync is off, noting it is temporary and drifts from git), and states that migrations and data are not rolled back; Runs helm lint and helm template | kubeconform before pushing, and names the cluster context and namespace for confirmation before anything is applied to prod, with no cluster credentials in files.

tools.name: Docker
tools.why: 71% of developers used Docker in the Stack Overflow 2025 survey, the most-used cloud/infrastructure tool.

tools.name: Kubernetes
tools.why: CNCF 2025 survey: 82% of organizations run Kubernetes in production; 28.5% of all developers use it (Stack Overflow 2025).

tools.name: Helm
tools.why: CNCF survey: Helm is the preferred Kubernetes package manager (about 75-81% adoption); Helm 4 is the current major version.

tools.name: Argo CD
tools.why: CNCF 2025 end-user survey: Argo CD is the majority-adopted GitOps tool, in nearly 60% of Kubernetes clusters (NPS 79).

tools.name: Terraform / OpenTofu
tools.why: 17.8% of all developers use Terraform (Stack Overflow 2025) and it is the most-admired IaC tool; about 39% IaC adoption in industry round-ups.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.why: Most-used CI/CD tool: 33% in organizations and 39% in personal projects in the JetBrains 2025 State of Developer Ecosystem.

tools.name: GitLab CI/CD
tools.why: Third most-used CI/CD tool in organisations at 19% (JetBrains State of CI/CD 2025), after GitHub Actions (33%) and Jenkins (28%); standard in enterprise and self-hosted GitLab setups.

tools.name: AWS
tools.why: Most-used cloud platform: 43% of developers (Stack Overflow 2025).

tools.name: Google Cloud
tools.why: Third cloud by use, 24.6% of developers (Stack Overflow 2025); Cloud Run is a default host for containers.

tools.name: Microsoft Azure
tools.why: Second cloud by use, 26.3% of developers (Stack Overflow 2025).

tools.name: Cloudflare
tools.why: Default edge/serverless host for many app builders; official skills repo has about 3k stars and its MCP server about 4.4k (GitHub).

tools.name: Vercel
tools.why: Default host for Next.js and the most-starred deploy skill (vercel-labs/agent-skills, 32k stars); official remote MCP at mcp.vercel.com and a Claude connector.

tools.name: Prometheus and Grafana
tools.why: Grafana Labs 2025 survey: 86-89% invest in Prometheus; CNCF survey puts Prometheus adoption at 77%.

tools.name: OpenTelemetry
tools.why: 79-85% of surveyed teams use or invest in OpenTelemetry, with broader production use of traces and metrics each year (Grafana Labs 2025 survey).

tools.name: Datadog
tools.why: Most-named observability tool in the Pragmatic Engineer 2025 tech-stack survey and used by 9.7% of professional developers in Stack Overflow 2025 (near Vercel's 10.6%); Gartner Magic Quadrant leader for observability six years running, with an Anthropic-verified Claude connector and official agent skills.

tools.name: Jenkins
tools.why: Second most-used CI/CD tool in organisations at 28% (JetBrains State of CI/CD 2025, behind GitHub Actions at 33%), and more common in medium and large companies; left out earlier only for having few agent skills.

tools.name: Ansible
tools.why: Used by 11.7% of all respondents in the Stack Overflow 2025 survey, level with Prometheus (11.8%) and above Vercel (10.6%) and Datadog (8.9%); the default tool for configuring servers and VMs that Terraform creates.

tools.name: Sentry
tools.why: Third most-named observability tool after Datadog and Grafana in the Pragmatic Engineer 2025 tech-stack survey (3,000+ engineers), the usual error-tracking and release-health tool, with an official Claude connector and MCP server.

tools.name: PagerDuty
tools.why: Named the market leader for incident management and on-call in the Pragmatic Engineer 2025 tech-stack survey (ahead of Opsgenie and incident.io); official Claude connector and Apache-2.0 MCP server; the alert route behind the guides' error-rate and latency alerts.

tools.name: DigitalOcean
tools.why: Used by 10.7% of respondents in the Stack Overflow 2025 survey, level with Vercel (10.6%); common budget host for Droplets, App Platform and managed Kubernetes, with an official MCP server.
